# Grouped bar graphs {#sec-grp-bar-graphs}


```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_jurassic(
    base_size = 15))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_jurassic()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_jurassic()`, modeled on the Jurassic Park (1993) Post Office souvenir stamp sheet: a black sheet with a logo red frame, a dark jungle plot area, stamp yellow titles, red, yellow, sunset orange, cream, and tan marks, and a Herculanum title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a categorical variable**      
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**
:::

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1993)
jp_dinos <- tibble(
  species = c("Brachiosaurus", "Triceratops", "Tyrannosaurus",
              "Gallimimus", "Velociraptor"),
  n = c(3, 5, 2, 20, 8),
  mean_tons = c(40, 9, 8, 0.45, 0.15),
  sd_tons = c(5, 1.2, 1, 0.08, 0.03)) |>
  tidyr::uncount(n) |>
  mutate(weight_tons = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_tons, sd = sd_tons), 2)) |>
  select(species, weight_tons)
jp_paddocks <- jp_dinos |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(total_tons = sum(weight_tons)) |>
  ungroup()
labs_grp_col <- labs(
    title = "Jurassic Park",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = "Total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock",
    x = "Paddock",
    y = "Total weight (tons)")
ggp2_grp_col <- ggplot(data = jp_paddocks,
              aes(x = species, 
                  y = total_tons)) + 
        geom_col(aes(fill = species),
            show.legend = FALSE) +
        scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2))
ggp2_grp_col + 
    labs_grp_col
```

::::

## Description 

A grouped bar graph uses bars to compare numbers across groups. Each group has its own set of bars standing next to each other. The words along the `x` axis name the groups, and the `y` axis gives the values.[^axis-labels] Colors or marks inside the bars show which smaller group each bar stands for,[^subsets] and a key on the side or top of the graph tells us which color goes with which group.[^legend]

`geom_col()` lets us show 'grouped' numbers for each group[^levels] in a column that puts each row in a group.[^categorical]

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

Bring in the code we'll use.[^packages]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_grp_col
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
library(tidyr) # for uncount()
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

A dinosaur is a living thing that walked the earth a very long time ago. *Jurassic Park* (1993) is a movie about a park full of living dinosaurs. A paddock is a piece of land with a wall around it. In the park, every kind[^species] of dinosaur lives in its own paddock. The park has five kinds of dinosaur: Brachiosaurus, Triceratops, Tyrannosaurus, Gallimimus, and Velociraptor. We'll make up[^simulate] the weight of every dinosaur in the park: each kind gets a number of dinosaurs (`n`) and its own rule for weights (`mean_tons` and `sd_tons`).[^distribution] `tidyr::uncount()` turns each row into `n` rows (one row for each dinosaur). A hill is a line that is high in the middle and low on both sides. `rnorm()` picks each dinosaur's weight from the hill for its kind.[^normal] Then we add up the weights in each paddock (`total_tons`). Starting with `set.seed()`[^seed] means you'll get the same dinosaurs every time you run the code below.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_grp_col
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1993) # same dinosaur weights every time the code runs
jp_dinos <- tibble(
  species = c("Brachiosaurus", "Triceratops", "Tyrannosaurus", # five species in the park
              "Gallimimus", "Velociraptor"),
  n = c(3, 5, 2, 20, 8), # number of animals of each species
  mean_tons = c(40, 9, 8, 0.45, 0.15), # average weight (tons)
  sd_tons = c(5, 1.2, 1, 0.08, 0.03) # spread of each species' weights
  ) |>
  tidyr::uncount(n) |> # one row per animal
  mutate(
    weight_tons = round(rnorm(n(), mean = mean_tons, sd = sd_tons), 2) # each animal's weight
    ) |>
  select(species, weight_tons)
jp_paddocks <- jp_dinos |>
  group_by(species) |> # one group per species
  summarise(total_tons = sum(weight_tons)) |> # total weight in each paddock
  ungroup()
glimpse(jp_paddocks)
```
:::

## Distribution

A grouped bar graph shows one number for each group, and here that number is a total. Each total comes from two things: how many dinosaurs live in a paddock and how heavy each one is. 20 Gallimimus are still lighter than two Tyrannosaurs. Below we'll move from the dinosaurs, to a graph, to the rule behind it.[^formula]

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first six dinosaurs.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_grp_col
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
head(jp_dinos, 6)
```
:::

A ton is a way of saying how heavy something is; a small car is about one ton. Each Brachiosaurus is close to 40 tons, and each Triceratops is close to 9. For every paddock, the total is the number of dinosaurs times their average weight.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_grp_col
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
jp_dinos |> 
  group_by(species) |> 
  summarise(
    dinosaurs = n(), 
    mean_tons = mean(weight_tons),
    total_tons = sum(weight_tons))
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

Each bar in a grouped bar graph is a bar model: a total made of parts. Below we show every dinosaur as its own piece and put the pieces in each paddock on top of each other.[^stack] How high each bar stands is the paddock's total, and the number of pieces is the number of dinosaurs in it. The Gallimimus bar has 20 small pieces, and the Brachiosaurus bar has three large ones.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_grp_col
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggplot(data = jp_dinos, 
    aes(x = species, y = weight_tons, fill = species)) + 
  geom_col(color = "#111111", linewidth = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) + 
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) + 
  labs(x = "Paddock", y = "Total weight (tons)")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

Each dinosaur's weight comes from a [hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution) for its kind,[^normal-2] $X_i \sim \text{Normal}(\mu, \sigma)$. A paddock's total adds up $n$ of these weights:

$$
T = X_1 + X_2 + \dots + X_n \sim \text{Normal}(n\mu, \; \sqrt{n}\,\sigma)
$$

The total we expect is $n\mu$:[^expected] $3 \times 40 = 120$ tons for the Brachiosaurus paddock and $20 \times 0.45 = 9$ tons for Gallimimus. How far the total often moves from that number[^spread] grows with $\sqrt{n}$, not $n$, because heavy and light dinosaurs even each other out in part. Our Brachiosaurus paddock comes to `r round(sum(jp_dinos$weight_tons[jp_dinos$species == "Brachiosaurus"]), 1)` tons, and the 120 we expect is less than one step[^sd] ($\sqrt{3} \times 5 \approx 8.7$ tons) away.

Try changing the number of each kind in `n`. Two times as many Velociraptors makes their bar two times as high, but the bar would still be the shortest in the park.


## Grammar

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

A grouped bar graph expects the number for each bar (the value that sets how long the bar is) to be in a column, and that column to be joined to `x` or `y`.[^measure]

  -   Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()`

  -   Start the graph with `ggplot()` and give it `data`

  -   Put `species` on the `x` axis and `total_tons` on the `y` axis[^map-xy]

  -   Join `species` to `fill`[^map-fill] *inside* the `aes()` of `geom_col()` 

  -   Put the long paddock names on two lines, moving every other name down,[^stagger] with `scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2))`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_grp_col
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true 
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_grp_col <- labs(
    title = "Jurassic Park",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = "Total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock",
    x = "Paddock",
    y = "Total weight (tons)")
ggp2_grp_col <- ggplot(data = jp_paddocks,
              aes(x = species, 
                  y = total_tons)) + 
        geom_col(aes(fill = species),
            show.legend = FALSE) +
        scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2))
ggp2_grp_col + 
    labs_grp_col
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_grp_col
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_grp_col <- labs(
    title = "Jurassic Park",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = "Total weight of the dinosaurs in each paddock",
    x = "Paddock",
    y = "Total weight (tons)")
ggp2_grp_col <- ggplot(data = jp_paddocks,
              aes(x = species, 
                  y = total_tons)) + 
        geom_col(aes(fill = species),
            show.legend = FALSE) +
        scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2))
ggp2_grp_col + 
    labs_grp_col
```


## More info

We didn't have to work out `total_tons` (shown on the `y` axis) for each `species`, because `ggplot2` does this for us!

If we give `x` a column of groups[^categorical-x] (like `species`) and give `y` a column of numbers[^continuous] (like `weight_tons`), `geom_col()` puts the rows in each group on top of each other,[^stack-col] which adds up `y` for each group in `x`:[^level-x]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: create_summary_sum_col_graph
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
jp_dinos |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = weight_tons)) + 
        geom_col(aes(fill = species),
            show.legend = FALSE) + 
        scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 2)) + 
  labs_grp_col
```
:::


We can see the totals behind the bars with the `group_by()` and `summarise()` steps[^functions] from `dplyr`.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: create_summary_sum_col
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
jp_dinos |> 
    dplyr::group_by(species) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
        `Total weight (tons)` = sum(weight_tons)
        ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |> 
    dplyr::select(`Paddock` = species, 
        `Total weight (tons)`)
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: show_summary_sum_col
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| layout-nrow: 1
jp_dinos |> 
    dplyr::group_by(species) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
        `Total weight (tons)` = sum(weight_tons)
        ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |> 
    dplyr::select(`Paddock` = species, 
        `Total weight (tons)`) |> 
    knitr::kable() |> 
    kableExtra::kable_minimal()
```
:::

[^axis-labels]: The x axis labels show the categories, and the y axis shows the values.

[^subsets]: Colors or patterns differentiate subsets.

[^legend]: The legend.

[^levels]: Levels of a variable.

[^categorical]: A categorical variable.

[^packages]: Install and load the packages.

[^species]: Species.

[^simulate]: Simulate.

[^distribution]: A normal distribution of weights for each species, set by `mean_tons` (the mean) and `sd_tons` (the standard deviation).

[^normal]: A normal distribution. `rnorm()` draws each weight from the normal distribution for its species.

[^seed]: Setting the random seed.

[^formula]: The formula.

[^stack]: Stacking (`geom_col()` stacks bars in the same `x` position by default), with each dinosaur as one segment.

[^normal-2]: A normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$ for each species.

[^expected]: The expected value of the total.

[^spread]: The spread (standard deviation) of the total.

[^sd]: One standard deviation of the total, $\sqrt{n}\,\sigma$.

[^measure]: Grouped bar graphs assume the statistical measure (the value the length of the bars is derived from) is contained in a variable and mapped to the `x` or `y` aesthetic.

[^labels]: Create the labels (title, subtitle, caption, and axis titles).

[^map-xy]: Map `species` to the `x` aesthetic and `total_tons` to the `y` aesthetic.

[^map-fill]: Map `species` to the `fill` aesthetic.

[^stagger]: Stagger (dodge) the axis labels over two rows.

[^categorical-x]: A categorical variable.

[^continuous]: A continuous variable.

[^stack-col]: Stacks the rows in each group.

[^level-x]: Each level of `x`.

[^functions]: Functions.
